messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testUnsafeDeSerialization` is testing the behavior of MultiValueMap deserialization when using unsafe classes. The test first creates a MultiValueMap using a safe collection class (ArrayList), serializes and deserializes it without issues. Then it creates another MultiValueMap with a presumably unsafe class (String class), serializes it and tries to deserialize it again. The test expects an UnsupportedOperationException on deserialization of the unsafe class.

Looking at the code snippet of MultiValueMap.multiValueMap(Map, Class), it creates a MultiValueMap instance by passing a ReflectionFactory constructed with the given class (collectionClass). The constructor of MultiValueMap stores the collection factory but does no validation or checks for unsafe types.

The bug report describes a remote code execution vulnerability due to deserialization of collections with unsafe classes through misuse of InvokerTransformer and similar attack vectors used with remote Java deserialization endpoints.

The test is failing because the current MultiValueMap does not prevent deserialization of unsafe collection classes, which could be exploited for remote code execution. The deserialized unsafe class (e.g., String) is accepted, instead of throwing the expected exception. The MultiValueMap internally uses the Factory for collections which appears to be constructed without any whitelist or validation of safe collection types.

Recent bug reports are unrelated or minor and do not address this issue.

Thus the root cause is that MultiValueMap or possibly the ReflectionFactory used to instantiate collections during deserialization does not enforce restrictions on allowed classes. The code lacks safeguards to prevent instantiation of arbitrary or unsafe collection classes on deserialization, which leads to the observed failure and the security vulnerability described.

Next, to confirm this, it is useful to inspect the ReflectionFactory class and see if it performs any validation on the class being instantiated. If not, that is where the validation should be added to prevent unsafe classes from being used with MultiValueMap deserialization.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
